findings.message: BQ79616-Q1 has no integrated current-sense ADC, so pack current is a separate channel with its own shunt, amplifier, rail and connector — and, more importantly, its own sample clock. Current and voltage sampled on unrelated clocks cannot be combined into a defensible SOC estimate; if SOC matters, budget the alignment work now or specify BQ75614-Q1 / BQ79656-Q1 instead.

The monitor stack is referenced to the accumulator, on the tractive-system side of the isolation boundary. The host UART crosses into the grounded low-voltage system and needs a digital isolator with an isolated supply on the pack side. The daisy-chain between boards is already differential and isolated; the host link is the one that usually is not, because it is the one that gets added last during bring-up. Isolation has not been declared either way.

NFAULT is a hardware fault line already routed to the host header. If fault status is only read inside the poll loop, the firmware learns about an over-voltage up to one poll period late — 100 ms at 10 Hz, during which nothing has reacted. Wiring it to an interrupt-capable GPIO costs one pin and one handler and decouples fault latency from logging rate. It does not replace the hardware shutdown path, which stays hardware.

Thermistor count per board not declared. Each device has 8 GPIO channels usable for pack temperature, and pack temperature is the measurement the thermal model needs and the rules care about. Unpopulated is a legitimate answer; blank is not.

Passive balancing not declared. It is not free: the internal FETs dissipate into the module, which is a thermal load on the pack the cooling model does not currently include, and the duty cycle is a parameter someone has to choose rather than inherit.

The cell-voltage resolution the balancing decision needs is not declared, so 190.73 uV/LSB cannot be judged adequate or excessive. 'The datasheet number is small' is not the same as 'small enough for the decision we make with it'.

Per-device response framing overhead has not been measured, and it is not published in the EVM guide or in SLVAE86B — both document command frames and defer the response layout to the data sheet's Command and Response Protocol section. Assuming 3-8 B/device, the response is 108-128 bytes and the poll ceiling is 66-78 Hz. findings.message: Per-device response framing overhead has not been measured, and it is not published in the EVM guide or in SLVAE86B — both document command frames and defer the response layout to the data sheet's Command and Response Protocol section. Assuming 3-8 B/device, the response is 1050-1200 bytes and the poll ceiling is 16-19 Hz. Measure it: one broadcast read of the cell block, count the bytes back, feed the count to measure_response_overhead(). Five minutes, and it turns every figure here from a range into a number.

17.605 Hz fits if the framing overhead is at the low end and does not if it is at the high end — the ceiling is somewhere in 16-19 Hz and the answer depends entirely on a constant nobody has measured. This is deliberately not resolved by picking a midpoint: the design either fits or it does not, and a five-minute bench measurement decides it. Until then, plan against 16 Hz.

findings.message: Per-device response framing overhead has not been measured, and it is not published in the EVM guide or in SLVAE86B — both document command frames and defer the response layout to the data sheet's Command and Response Protocol section. Assuming 3-8 B/device, the response is 46-56 bytes and the poll ceiling is 138-163 Hz. Measure it: one broadcast read of the cell block, count the bytes back, feed the count to measure_response_overhead(). Five minutes, and it turns every figure here from a range into a number.

500 Hz polling is not achievable at any plausible framing overhead: the link tops out at 163 Hz even in the best case. The response is 46-56 bytes and it grows linearly with board count, so this does not improve with tuning. Either raise the baud rate to at least about 354 kbaud, poll a shorter register block, or accept the lower rate. Note that the rate people quote for this bridge is usually chosen before anyone multiplies board count by payload.
